Title: July 23, 2026 - Boulder City Council Special Meeting (Airport Funding and BVCP Public Hearings)
Overview: The Boulder City Council special meeting focused on airport funding and the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan. Council unanimously approved the consent agenda, moved the BVCP adoption hearing to August 6, and heard staff financial scenarios, legal advice on FAA obligations, and dozens of public comments on the airport's future. After amendment, council voted 8-1 to continue airport operations, with council approval required for the next FAA grant that carries perpetuity obligations. Councilmember Wallik also announced his resignation at the end of the meeting.

Topic1.Title: Agenda amendments and consent agenda approval
Topic1.Summary: Council voted unanimously to amend the agenda, removing the BVCP adoption from the agenda and adding items for special counsel appointment and holding the July 30 meeting in person. The consent agenda (items 2A through 2F) was then approved unanimously after brief questions about ballot measure language and a special counsel appointment for code of conduct complaints.

Topic2.Title: BVCP public hearing continued to August 6
Topic2.Summary: Council opened the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan adoption public hearing, which staff introduced before council moved to continue it to August 6. The motion passed unanimously and the item was removed from tonight's deliberations.

Topic3.Title: Airport continued operation: staff presentation and financial scenarios
Topic3.Summary: Staff presented financial scenarios for continued airport operations, including options with and without FAA grants and a range of projected deficits. Staff noted that FAA obligations may extend in perpetuity for land-acquisition grants and that a state infrastructure bank loan is the only alternative financing identified. Options for landing fees, hangar development, solar, and other revenue were reviewed, though none were seen as fully closing the gap.

Topic4.Title: Council questions on airport legal options and closure
Topic4.Summary: Council asked outside counsel about the legal and practical implications of FAA obligations, including perpetuity, litigation timelines and costs, and the possibility of closure through litigation, congressional action, or a replacement airport. Counsel described the process as complex, with low probability and costly litigation paths, and staff noted that the 2017 Santa Monica litigation took about 10 years and roughly $10 million.

Topic5.Title: Public hearing testimony on airport future
Topic5.Summary: Dozens of residents, pilots, business representatives, and neighbors testified. Supporters emphasized emergency response, flight training, youth aviation programs, science research, and economic activity, while opponents raised concerns about noise, lead pollution, perpetual FAA obligations, land use, and the need for a public vote. Testimony also addressed landing fees, unleaded fuel, and comparisons to Santa Monica and Longmont.

Topic6.Title: Council deliberation and votes on FAA grant acceptance
Topic6.Summary: Council members discussed fiscal responsibility, budget pressures, noise, climate, and the risk of perpetuity obligations. A motion to require a one-year delay on perpetuity-covenant FAA grants failed 6-3, and a motion to approve continued operation was amended to require council approval of the next FAA grant with perpetuity obligations, which passed 6-3. The amended motion then passed 8-1 after a further vote. Councilmember Wallik announced his resignation at the end of the meeting.
